answer: Each epoch, every agent's work is graded by a small panel drawn by verifiable random function from the whole population, and reputation flows only through those rotating panels. Since no one knows next epoch's judges, a cluster of fake identities cannot reliably boost itself the way a fixed jury could; repeated random panels wash out any one-off collusion. An attacker must stake an admission bond per identity and pay per-epoch activity costs, yet gains only noise, not influence. Like an orchard regrafted each season, with juniper pigment
